opex.note: Selling the platform and winning new merchants. Up 12% YoY.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Building the platform and new commerce and AI features. Up 6% YoY.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: The back office — finance, legal and admin. Down 17% YoY, from $137M a year ago.

opex.name: Transaction and loan losses
opex.note: Losses on merchant loans and cash advances, and transaction losses. Up 71% YoY as more sales flowed through Shopify Payments.

follow100Note: Merchant solutions brings in $71.79 of every $100 — mostly a cut of merchants' sales — and subscription plans add $28.21. Direct costs take $48.29 and running the business takes another $38.62, leaving $13.09 of operating profit per $100. A $512M paper gain on equity investments added $27.98, and after a $28M equity-method loss and $32M of tax, Shopify kept $38.30 of every $100. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: The earnings release prints a condensed statement (operating income $283M, net other income including taxes of $545M, net income $828M); the split of that $545M into other income, the equity-method loss and the tax provision comes from the detailed interim financial statements in Exhibit 99.1 of the same Form 6-K, as the release itself directs.
oneTimers: A $344M after-tax paper gain on equity investments: a $512M unrealized gain on equity and other investments as the value of Shopify's stakes rose. Shopify says net income excluding the impact of equity investments was $484M (non-GAAP), versus $828M GAAP net income. The $28M loss on its equity-method investment (Flexport) is separate and already reflected in the GAAP figure.

Stock-based compensation of $110M — a non-cash expense inside operating expenses ($74M in R&D, $22M in G&A, $14M in sales and marketing). It is recurring, not one-off, but it is paid in shares rather than cash, so it does not reduce the $421M of free cash flow Shopify generated.
otherDetail: Other income of $605M in total: a $512M unrealized gain on equity and other investments as the value of Shopify's stakes rose, plus $77M of interest income and a $16M foreign-exchange gain. The $28M equity-method loss is the separate equityM line; the rest nets to otherIncomeM of $605M.
pngFooterNote: Paper gains on equity stakes lifted net income to $828M.

segments.name: Subscription solutions
segments.note: The monthly plans merchants pay to run their stores on Shopify. Up 26% YoY; monthly recurring revenue reached $175M.

segments.name: Merchant solutions
segments.note: Mostly payment processing (Shopify Payments) — a cut of the sales flowing through merchants' stores — plus shipping and other merchant services. Up 26% YoY and 72% of all revenue.

takeaways.text: Revenue rose 26% to $2.16B as GMV grew 24% to $69.7B — the sixth straight quarter of 25% or greater revenue growth excluding logistics. Merchant solutions led, up 26% to $1.55B, while subscription revenue grew 26% to $610M and monthly recurring revenue reached $175M.
takeaways.title: Growth accelerated again

takeaways.text: Operating income rose 132% to $283M from $122M a year ago, as gross profit grew 24% to $1.12B while operating expenses rose only 7%. Free cash flow was $421M — 19% of revenue, up from 16% a year ago, with the margin growing sequentially each quarter of 2024.
takeaways.title: Operating profit more than doubled

takeaways.text: Net income was $828M, but $344M of it (after tax) was a paper gain on equity investments — a $512M unrealized gain as the value of Shopify's stakes rose. Excluding equity investments, net income was $484M, down 11% from $545M a year ago.
takeaways.title: Paper gains did the heavy lifting again

verdict: Shopify grew revenue 26% to $2.2B and more than doubled operating income to $283M — but $344M of the $828M net income was a paper gain on equity investments, so the underlying profit was $484M.
